newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Salvadorean Congress vetoes telephone company sale.
newsitem.headline: Salvadorean Congress vetoes telephone company sale.

text.p: El Salvador's legislature vetoed the government's privatization bill for the state telephone company, legislators said on Friday.
The veto passed on Thursday night with the vote of 56 opposition party legistors, while 28 legislators from the ruling pary abstained.
Legislators from ruling right-wing Republican National Alliance (ARENA) said on Friday that they will launch a national campaign to support the law.
El Salvador president Armando Calderon Sol can overrule the veto and uphold the bill.
Still, the show of power from the opposition party is a blow to the ARENA, who lost the legislative majority in March.
"It is a historic message...that the will of the Salvadoreans must be respected," the head of former guerrilla political party Farabundi Marti National Liberation Front Shafick Handal said.
ARENA deputy Gloria Salguero warned, "Halting modernization will cause the country to face grave problems."
Thursday's vote followed bitter debate, with attending telephone workers intermittently applauding and booing legislators.

The National Telecommunications Administration (ANTEL) is supporting the privatization, calling it a means of modernizing the company. The winning buyer is expected to invest $3 billion in the company in the next ten years.
ANTEL was been priced at between $300 million and $1 billion.
Sources at ANTEL have said the company has a deficit of 300,000 telephone lines, with only 4.5 lines per 100 Salvadoreans compared with a demand of 40 lines per 100 residents.
